meta.name: ML-training-operations agent benchmark
meta.question: Can agents do ML training operations (distributed jobs, checkpoints, OOMs, stragglers, Kubernetes quotas, torchtitan), and does the serving setup of a self-hosted model change how many they solve?
meta.domain: ML infrastructure / training operations (fault diagnosis and repair in sandboxed multi-process jobs)
meta.status_reason: Stopped building frontier-hard tasks on Oct 13, 2026: across five rounds (v1, v2, v3, titan-fork-drift, titan-silent-divergence), Codex with OpenAI models solved 88-100% of every round, so the tasks have no headroom as a frontier capability test. The self-hosted result stands: on the same tasks a 27B open model's solve rate moves 15-25 points with GPU, load and serving settings.

run_dates.note: Self-hosted runs Oct 10, 12 and 13; vendor-API runs Oct 12-13 (attempts.jsonl, api_attempts*.jsonl).

dataset.source: Tasks built for this benchmark: injected faults in multi-process training setups, each graded by an independent test (Harbor task format). Families from published failure taxonomies (ByteRobust, L4, SIGMA).
dataset.url_note: Not published; tasks live in the repo (mlops_tasks/, mlops_hard/tasks/).
dataset.license_note: Own tasks; no license chosen. titan tasks contain a modified fork of torchtitan v0.2.2 (check torchtitan's license before publishing).
dataset.dropped_reason: None dropped. Every task was validated: the reference (oracle) solution passes and a no-op agent fails on Modal.
dataset.split_note: No split; all tasks are evaluation tasks. Later rounds were designed after seeing earlier results.
dataset.types_note: Hard set = 8 tasks (2 per family A-D); v2 set = 3 new tasks (exact-resume, k8s-quota-zone, two-stragglers) plus atomic-checkpoint; 'hard + v2' = 11 tasks.

setup.tools: Harness's own tools in a Modal sandbox per task (terminus-2: tmux; mini-swe-agent: bash; Codex and Claude Code: their CLIs' tools). CPU sandboxes (4 CPU, 8 GB for hard/v2/v3; 2 CPU, 4 GB for v1); torchtitan tasks get 8 CPU, 32 GB and 2 GPUs (L40S per mlops_bench_plan.md).

judges.name: task test
judges.type: deterministic test per task (recomputes results, fault injection, hidden seeds, golden loss curves for torchtitan)

grading.self_grading_check: No model grades. Each task validated with oracle (pass) and no-op agent (fail); three hard-set tasks also checked with a partial fix that fails.

metrics.name: accuracy (solve rate)
metrics.definition: solved trials / attempted trials, pooled over runs of the condition.

metrics.name: cost_per_correct_cents (self-hosted)
metrics.definition: 100 x sum of (gpu_cost_usd + sandbox_cost_est_usd) / solved trials; gpu_cost_usd = run seconds / 3600 x $/GPU-hour (H100 $3.95, H200 $4.54); sandbox estimate = trial seconds x (CPUs x $0.1419 + GiB x $0.024) per hour.

metrics.name: cost_per_correct_cents (vendor API)
metrics.definition: 100 x api_cost_usd / solved trials; api_cost per trial = max(harness-reported cost, ((input - cached) x input price + cached x cached price + output x output price) / 1e6). Task sandboxes not included.

metrics.name: ci95
metrics.definition: 95% bootstrap interval of the solve rate resampling tasks with all their trials (2000 resamples, seed 0); null with fewer than 2 tasks.

metrics.name: mean_calls_per_case
metrics.definition: mean agent steps per trial (self-hosted, from trajectories); not recorded for API runs.

noise.method: Every self-hosted hard-set setup run twice (rep 0/1, 3 attempts per task each) except the 4k/16k caps and the MoE model.
noise.size: Identical self-hosted runs differed by up to 7 solves of 24 (mini-swe-agent, reasoning off: 8/24 vs 15/24); defaults repeated at 17/24 and 17/24 (terminus-2) and 14/24 and 17/24 (mini-swe-agent).
noise.ci_method: Paired bootstrap over the 8 tasks (mlops_hard_analysis.py, 10000 resamples, seed 0) for differences vs H100 defaults at 24 agents.
noise.tie_threshold: A paired 95% CI that includes 0 is no difference; the plan treats single-run differences of 3 or fewer solves out of 24 as noise.

results_note: Keys: 'self-hosted | <task set> | <harness> | <config> | cN' and 'vendor API | <task round> | <harness> | <model>'. Every attempted trial is in n; timeouts, harness errors and setup failures count as unsolved. Excluded: one self-hosted run that recorded no trials (excluded_runs). Vendor-API runs: the Claude Code + Claude Haiku 5.5 hard-set run failed in setup on every trial (0/8, all NonZeroAgentExitCodeError) and stays in n; a second Claude Code + Haiku 5.5 run (job tagged mlops_hard2, 1 attempt) recorded only 2 trials (atomic-checkpoint, corrupt-shard), 1 passed, and Harbor exited with code 130 (interrupted).
per_type_note: Types are task families (A-D for the hard and v2 tasks) or rounds (v1 pilot, v3, real-system).

paired_comparisons.note: Computed with mlops_hard_analysis.py's per_task and boot (reward.txt per trial). Hard set: each setup vs H100 defaults at 24 agents with both runs pooled, 8 tasks. v2 set: H200 vs H100 at 24 agents, one run each, 4 tasks.

headline_findings.finding: On the 8-task hard set, an H200 instead of an H100 at 24 agents raised Qwen3.8-27B's solve rate by 22.92 points with terminus-2 and 18.75 with mini-swe-agent.
A one-flag server cap of 8,192 output tokens per call raised mini-swe-agent's solve rate by 14.58 points and gave terminus-2 its lowest H100 cost per solve.

limitations: Small task sets: 6 (v1), 8 (hard), 4 (v2), 5 (v3), 2 (torchtitan); bootstrap CIs over 4-8 tasks are wide.
Tasks were built by the same team that ran the agents, and later rounds were designed after seeing earlier results.
One self-hosted model family (Qwen3.8-27B, plus one MoE run per harness) on one engine (vLLM 0.31.0).

Frontier coverage is mostly OpenAI models through Codex; Anthropic runs failed in setup (Claude Code + Haiku 5.5: 0/8, all agent-exit errors) or were partial (2 trials recorded, 1 passed, Harbor exit code 130), so they say nothing about Anthropic models' ability.
API cost excludes Modal sandboxes (and the 2-GPU sandboxes of the torchtitan tasks); OpenAI prices come from third-party aggregators per api_runs.py.
v3 and torchtitan tasks were only run with frontier API models, not the self-hosted model.
The 4k/16k output caps and the MoE model are single runs.
Self-hosted failure categories come from Harbor exception types; they do not separate looping from working timeouts.
Sandbox cost for self-hosted runs is an estimate that under-counts the bill.
inconsistencies: BENCHMARKS.md says the hard set and v2/v3 total '18 tasks incl. titan'; mlops_hard/tasks has 18 task directories (8 hard + 3 v2 + 5 v3 + 2 titan), so with the 6 v1 tasks the benchmark has 24 tasks.
Two OpenAI runs over the same 11 tasks have job names tagged 'mlops_hard2' and 'mlops_hard' but task_set 'mlops_all' in api_attempts.jsonl; both ran all 11 tasks (pooled here).
mlops_bench_plan.md's frontier table and 'Every OpenAI model ... solves 88-100%' omit the Anthropic runs (0/8 setup failures; 1/2 partial).
mlops_bench_plan.md (Oct 10) reports +29 points (CI 8-50) for mini-swe-agent at 8 vs 24 agents from single runs; after repeats mlops_hard.md and this file give +25 (pooled baseline).
mlops_bench_plan.md 'Learnings' says mini-swe-agent gains '+6 points, CI [-6, +19]' from 60 minutes; the later table and mlops_hard.md give +6 [-2, +17].

BENCHMARKS.md says the open-model result is 'serving setup moves a 27B model's solve rate 15-25 pts'; on the v2 set the H200 effect is +37.5 (terminus-2) and +37.5 (mini-swe-agent) points (mlops_bench_plan.md: '+38').
Total spend is not separable: the plan quotes partial bills and running totals of the whole research project (not reproduced here) rather than this bench.
